title: Alternative-Geometry Attacks on Unbalanced Feistel Schemes
summary: For unbalanced Feistel schemes with expanding functions, the examined multi-rectangle approach fails; find a generic attack improving on both two-point and rectangle attacks.

formal_statement.body: For unbalanced Feistel schemes with expanding functions, construct a generic attack that improves upon both the two-point attack $\mathrm{TWO}$ and the rectangle attacks $\mathrm{R1}$, $\mathrm{R2}$, $\mathrm{R3}$, $\mathrm{R4}$ by employing alternative equation geometries---such as hexagons, multidimensional cubes, or linked multi-rectangles---in place of the standard two-dimensional rectangles. The key challenge is that the multi-rectangle approach has been shown to fail, and most other alternative geometries investigated so far have not outperformed the rectangle-based attacks; some variants remain under investigation, leaving this construction as an open problem.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of generic attacks on unbalanced Feistel schemes with expanding functions.
parameters: Equation geometry: the structural arrangement varied to seek improvement over standard two-dimensional rectangles
scope.unresolved_remainder: Construct a working generic attack using an alternative equation geometry that improves upon both TWO and the R1, R2, R3, and R4 rectangle attacks.

citations.label: Improved Generic Attacks on Unbalanced Feistel Schemes with Expanding Functions

progress.summary: The source calls designing attacks better than two-point or rectangle attacks an interesting problem and describes trials with alternative equation geometries. Its illustrative multi-rectangle example does not work, and multi-rectangle attacks remain under investigation.
citation_labels: Emmanuel Volte et al., Improved Generic Attacks on Unbalanced Feistel Schemes with Expanding Functions
